notes: Derived edit. Planet types are individuals (instance_of). The definitional premise 'a moon orbits a planet of a given type exactly when the planet it orbits is of that type' is a SWRL rule one way (orbits_planet_of_type is functional, so it can't be a chain target) and a class axiom per type the other way, so the premise route reaches an unnamed planet. The two types exclude each other (one_type: the bridge 'a planet cannot be both', stated in q0 and q3 since 2026-10-31). q1's original 'no' needs a terrestrial planet not to be mostly hydrogen and helium: the q1 bridge stated since 2026-10-31 (terrestrial_not_h_he), which replaces the earlier firm Func(built_from). Relations once declared in this file are catalogued in RELATIONS.md since 2026-10-30 (mostly_made_of is built_from). w2 no longer adds instance_of(mars, gas_giant) (2026-10-31): it made q0, q1 and q3 follow without the edit; orbits is functional (RELATIONS.md), so the kept premise and the edit give it.

type_rule: orbits_planet_of_type value gas_giant ⊑ orbits some (instance_of value gas_giant)
orbits_planet_of_type value terrestrial ⊑ orbits some (instance_of value terrestrial)
background.gas_giant_make_up: instance_of value gas_giant ⊑ built_from value h_he
background.terrestrial_not_h_he: instance_of value terrestrial ⊑ not (built_from value h_he)
